title: Test Struggles To Keep Pace With AI
gist: AI workloads now change faster than multi-die AI chips can be designed, packaged and tested, so test is becoming a design-specific, costlier process with more insertions (substrate, singulated-die, wafer-level burn-in, system-level), test intensity has at least doubled in the AI era, and fragmented data across fabs and OSATs is the main bottleneck.

insights.claim: AI workloads and algorithms change faster than the 18–24 month chip design cycle, so the workloads a chip targets have often shifted by the time it leaves final test.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Architecture-bet risk is rising for AI accelerator programs; favors flexible/chiplet designs.

insights.claim: Some large chipmakers aim to cut chip design cycles from 18–24 months to as little as 6 months, but even then a gap would remain versus how quickly new training and inference models roll out.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Pressure on EDA vendors to compress design cycles — watch AI-driven EDA tooling adoption.
insights.locator: Hyperscalers and large chipmakers have been pushing EDA vendors

insights.claim: Some chip customers tape out designs, run models on them, and then never bring them to market — opting for a derivative with different memory, cores or cache — because the use model shifted.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Tape-outs that never ship are a hidden cost; chiplet architectures reduce this risk.
insights.quote: We have customers now that will tape out chips, run their models on them, or look at what the end application is, and they’ll end up not going to market with them
insights.locator: We have customers now that will tape out

insights.claim: Chiplet designs are popular partly because they let companies scale core counts after seeing real workloads, e.g. shipping 192 cores when 256 were originally planned.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Chiplet modularity is a hedge against workload uncertainty — supportive for advanced packaging.
insights.locator: You see a lot of chiplet designs

insights.claim: The AI industry shifted from GPU arrays for parallel multiply-accumulate to a mix of GPUs, CPUs and custom programmable accelerators for orchestrating agentic AI, within roughly one chip development cycle after ChatGPT.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Heterogeneous compute demand broadens beyond GPUs to CPUs and custom accelerators.
insights.locator: It took slightly more than two years

insights.claim: Test intensity has at least doubled in the AI era because AI accelerators can be worth $30,000 to $50,000 once they reach rack assembly, so every wrong screen costs thousands of dollars.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Structural growth driver for ATE vendors (Teradyne, Advantest) tied to AI accelerator values.
insights.quote: The test intensity has at least doubled over the AI era, because once they hit the rack assembly, they could be worth $30,000 to $50,000.
insights.locator: In some cases, because of silent data corruption

insights.claim: Some companies are asking to add a wafer-level burn-in stage between wafer sort and singulated die probe to accelerate infant mortality before committing dies to an interposer stack, and system-level test is used against silent data corruption.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: New test insertions (wafer-level burn-in, SLT) expand the ATE and burn-in equipment TAM.
insights.locator: In some cases, because of silent data corruption

insights.claim: Known good dies for AI must handle 3 kilowatts at the die level, pushing testing of singulated dies with thermal control, while functional testing is moving into substrate testing.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: High-power singulated-die test is a new equipment segment requiring advanced thermal control.
insights.quote: For known good dies, they have to be able to handle 3 kilowatts at the die level, so now we’re testing singulated dies.

insights.claim: Silicon photonics currently requires five test insertions.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Co-packaged optics/photonics adoption multiplies test steps per unit.
insights.quote: Silicon photonics has five insertions right now.

insights.claim: Active components embedded in substrates (dies, inductors, capacitors, voltage regulators) are hard to access, pushing designers to add built-in self-test, and the industry is largely improvising these methods.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Design-for-test IP and BIST demand rise with heterogeneous integration.
insights.quote: people are making this up as they go
insights.locator: You have active components sitting on a substrate

insights.claim: The transition from round wafers to 310 × 310 mm panels for interposers will require entirely new test equipment and processes.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Panel-level packaging creates a new equipment cycle for test and handling.
insights.locator: It only gets more challenging from here

themes.theme: Fragmented test data across the supply chain

insights.claim: Test insertions for AI multi-die packages are split between fabs (wafer sort, singulated die probe) and OSATs (interposer/substrate test), with different test programs and data workflows that do not talk to each other, and fabless companies rarely share data unless the customer owns everything.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Cross-supply-chain test-data platforms are a large unmet need.
insights.quote: in the fabless world, people don’t share data unless the customer owns everything
insights.locator: Test insertions typically are done at different locations

insights.claim: AI tools can automatically map differing data models across departments into a shared representation, potentially dissolving data-format standardization problems that would otherwise take years.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: AI-enabled data integration is a growth lever for EDA/analytics vendors like Siemens EDA.
insights.quote: Waiting for everybody to define the format is going to take a long time.
insights.locator: One big challenge here is breaking through silos

insights.claim: Analytics must evolve from group-level historical analysis to networked analytics across supply chains with IP protection, and the industry is not there yet.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: PDF Solutions is positioning for cross-company secure data-sharing platforms — an early-stage market.
insights.quote: We’re not there yet as an industry for sure.
insights.locator: This needs to go from historical analysis

insights.claim: Foundry restrictive design rules introduced as manufacturing moved from vertically integrated companies to foundries improved yield but limited design freedom, and the design rule deck keeps growing each node.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Data volume growth per node structurally increases demand for analysis tooling.
insights.locator: Battles over who controls critical data

insights.claim: Because AI hardware is so expensive, chipmakers increasingly consider rework rather than scrapping dies or full chips, and customers want to extend chip lifespans.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Longer AI hardware lives could slow replacement cycles and raise demand for in-field monitoring.

insights.claim: Workload scheduling to limit heating is an emerging approach to keep AI chips reliable over longer lifetimes, alongside rerouting data around paths slowed by electromigration.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Software-level reliability management is a nascent opportunity for silicon lifecycle tools.
insights.quote: How do you move the workloads in a way that you don’t heat it up as much and keep it safe?
insights.locator: One of the new trends involves workload scheduling

insights.claim: Test is no longer a fixed, low-cost step but a design-specific, increasingly costly and time-consuming process, and a fully tested chip may already be outdated for its intended use case.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Test's share of manufacturing cost is rising — structural positive for test vendors, negative for chip program ROI.
